blocker_detail: The wrapper skill itself only tells the user to run '/skills add johnpapa/ai-ready' inside GitHub Copilot CLI and explicitly says 'Do not run the command on the user's behalf' -- that specific mechanic (Copilot CLI's /skills installer) isn't available in this runtime and isn't something we're meant to run anyway. This did not block the actual underlying task: the real ai-ready skill also documents optional steps (0b-0d) that mine PR review history and community-health signals via the GitHub API/gh CLI with an authenticated account; those were skipped as out of scope for a fresh, unauthenticated local repo (no credentials used), but they are enhancements, not the core deliverable. The core deliverable -- analyzing a codebase and generating AGENTS.md, a copilot-instructions.md pointer, a CI workflow, and issue/PR templates -- was fully produced and verified locally without needing any external tool.
